title: Improved Convergence Rates for Stochastic Multi-Gradient Descent which Close the Gap: A Proof by AI
abstract: arXiv:2607.18174v2 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: For smooth nonconvex stochastic multi-objective optimization, stochastic multi-gradient descent (SMG) computes an approximate steepest common descent direction of the objectives from stochastic gradients. Under standard assumptions, this note establishes a new convergence rate for SMG in terms of the squared Pareto-stationarity (PS) measure. With a constant stepsize and linearly growing mini-batches, the expected squared empirical PS measure at the algorithm's output is $\tilde{O}(T^{-1})$ after $T$ iterations. This improves on the $\tilde{O}(T^{-1/4})$ bound obtained by Chen et al. (JMLR, 2024) for linearly growing batches, without requiring bounded gradients. Here, $\tilde{O}(\cdot)$ suppresses logarithmic factors. The key to the rate improvement is to exploit the Lipschitz continuity of the PS measure, defined by the norm of the multi-gradient descent algorithm (MGDA) direction, rather than the $(1/2)$-H\"older continuity of the MGD

translated_title: 随机多梯度 descent 的改进收敛速率——填补差距：由 AI 完成的证明
translated_abstract: 对于光滑非凸的随机多目标优化问题，随机多梯度下降（SMG）从随机梯度中计算各目标函数的近似最速公共下降方向。在标准假设下，本文针对 SMG 在平方帕累托平稳性（PS）度量方面建立了一个新的收敛速率：采用常数步长和线性增长的迷你批量，经过 $T$ 次迭代后，算法输出处的期望平方经验 PS 度量为 $\tilde{O}(T^{-1})$。这改进了 Chen 等人（JMLR, 2024）在线性增长批量下得到的 $\tilde{O}(T^{-1/4})$ 的界，且不需要有界梯度假设。其中 $\tilde{O}(\cdot)$ 隐藏了对数因子。收敛速率提升的关键在于利用由多梯度下降算法（MGDA）方向的范数所定义的 PS 度量的 Lipschitz 连续性，而非 MGDA 方向的 (1/2)-Hölder 连续性。
tldr: 本文通过利用帕累托平稳性度量的 Lipschitz 连续性（而非 (1/2)-Hölder 连续性），证明了随机多梯度下降（SMG）在常数步长和线性增长批量下可将平方帕累托平稳性度量的收敛速率从此前的 $\tilde{O}(T^{-1/4})$ 提升至 $\tilde{O}(T^{-1})$，且无需有界梯度假设。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that stochastic multi-gradient descent (SMG) achieves an improved $\tilde{O}(T^{-1})$ convergence rate in squared Pareto-stationarity measure with constant stepsize and linearly growing mini-batches—closing the gap with the previous $\tilde{O}(T^{-1/4})$ bound—by exploiting the Lipschitz continuity of the PS measure rather than its (1/2)-Hölder continuity, without requiring bounded gradients.
